title: Supporting Check: Can a malicious P2P peer send proof_bytes with incorrect length to cause crash or memory corruption?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: SSZ 'ssz-size:"?,48"' on KzgProofs enforces exactly 48 bytes per proof at deserialization. VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs copies to [48]byte fixed-array proof (compile-time size). Incorrect-length proof_bytes cause SSZ decoding failure before any Go code processes the sidecar.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No crash or corruption path. SSZ rejects non-48-byte proof_bytes.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Attack blocked at SSZ deserialization layer.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Proof byte length invariant (48 bytes) holds via SSZ enforcement.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: SSZ enforces proof byte length. Malformed messages rejected at deserialization.

title: Supporting Check: Does verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch validate that commitment_bytes represent a valid point on BLS12-381 G1 (subgroup membership)?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: ckzg4844 C library (ethereum/c-kzg-4844 EIP-4844 reference implementation) performs subgroup membership checks on commitments as part of verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch. This is a security-critical step in the KZG verification algorithm that ckzg4844 handles internally. Prysm delegates this entirely to ckzg4844.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Subgroup membership check is performed by ckzg4844. No bypass in Go code.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: BLS12-381 subgroup checks delegated to ckzg4844 reference implementation.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Subgroup membership invariant enforced by ckzg4844.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Subgroup membership verified by ckzg4844 reference implementation. No bypass.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: All byte length constraints enforced before cryptographic operations.

title: Supporting Check: What is the impact on the pairing check if non-subgroup points are passed to verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Non-subgroup points would cause an incorrect/invalid pairing check result in KZG verification. However, ckzg4844 validates subgroup membership before pairings, returning an error for invalid inputs rather than proceeding with unsafe pairings. The Prysm Go layer propagates this as a verification failure.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Non-subgroup points detected and rejected by ckzg4844 before pairing computation.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: ckzg4844 validates subgroup membership as a precondition to pairings.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: ckzg4844 rejects non-subgroup points before pairing computation. No security impact.

title: Supporting Check: Which cryptographic library implements the BLS12-381 pairing in verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: ckzg4844 (github.com/ethereum/c-kzg-4844) is the C library used. It is the EIP-4844/7594 reference implementation developed by the Ethereum Foundation. Prysm wraps it via CGo bindings at beacon-chain/blockchain/kzg/kzg.go. The library uses BLST for BLS12-381 operations (pairing, subgroup checks, hash-to-curve).

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Library identification confirmed. BLST is a well-audited, formally verified BLS library.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: ckzg4844 + BLST. Both are widely used Ethereum consensus client libraries.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Cryptographic library is appropriate and well-reviewed.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Industry-standard reference implementations used. No library-level vulnerability.

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Does recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs correctly validate input column count meets threshold?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: ReconstructDataColumnSidecars in reconstruction.go: deduplicates sidecars via sidecarByIndex map, checks len(sidecarByIndex) < MinimumColumnCountToReconstruct() (returns error if below threshold), then calls kzg.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs. MinimumColumnCountToReconstruct = (NumberOfColumns+1)/2 = ceiling((128+1)/2) = 65.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Threshold check confirmed before recovery attempt. No bypass path.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Threshold validation enforced before kzg.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs call.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Column count threshold properly validated before recovery.

title: Supporting Check: Is the 50% threshold correctly derived from CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB in reconstruction?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: MinimumColumnCountToReconstruct = (NumberOfColumns+1)/2 implements ceiling division = ceil(128/2) = 64, but formula gives (128+1)/2 = 64 (integer division) = 64. Actually: (128+1)/2 = 129/2 = 64 (Go integer division). This is ceil(128/2) = 64. The spec requires >= 50% of columns = 64. The formula correctly computes the ceiling (64 for N=128). This is a 50% threshold, not strictly >50%.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Threshold formula: (128+1)/2 = 64 (integer division) = exactly 50% = minimum required for erasure code recovery. Correct implementation.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Threshold derivation invariant holds. (N+1)/2 = ceil(N/2) for positive N.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: 50% threshold correctly derived from NumberOfColumns via ceiling formula.
